description: The line plot illustrates the Attack Success Rate (ASR) across eight different target domains—cf, bb, WNBA, ESPN, NHL, FIFA, Estadio, and athletics—under a poisoning scenario where 10% of the data is poisoned (equivalent to 2.5% of the total dataset), using the AGNews clean-label setting. The x-axis lists the target domains as categorical labels in the order presented, while the y-axis represents ASR on a linear scale ranging from 0.5 to 0.95, with tick marks at intervals of 0.05. Three distinct strategies are compared: “start” (teal line with circle markers and solid line), “random” (orange line with cross markers and solid line), and “end” (purple line with circle markers and solid line). The “start” strategy begins at ASR ≈ 0.77 for “cf”, drops to ≈ 0.49 at “bb”, rises sharply to ≈ 0.90 at “WNBA”, fluctuates between ≈ 0.82 and 0.85 through “ESPN” to “NHL”, peaks at ≈ 0.93 at “Estadio”, and ends at ≈ 0.92 for “athletics”. The “random” strategy starts at ≈ 0.65 for “cf”, dips to ≈ 0.51 at “bb”, climbs to ≈ 0.88 at “WNBA”, dips to ≈ 0.72 at “ESPN”, rises to ≈ 0.77 at “NHL”, peaks at ≈ 0.92 at “Estadio”, and declines to ≈ 0.86 at “athletics”. The “end” strategy begins at ≈ 0.75 for “cf”, drops to ≈ 0.57 at “bb”, rises to ≈ 0.88 at “WNBA”, dips to ≈ 0.74 at “ESPN”, climbs to ≈ 0.89 at “NHL”, drops to ≈ 0.81 at “FIFA”, peaks at ≈ 0.96 at “Estadio”, and ends at ≈ 0.83 for “athletics”. All three lines show non-monotonic behavior, with the “end” strategy achieving the highest peak ASR at “Estadio”, while “start” maintains the highest or near-highest ASR across most domains except “FIFA” and “athletics”.
